subject: Grounding sensitivity and retrieval tuning — Caspian Analytics next steps
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Amit Patel <amit@caspiananalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Grounding sensitivity and retrieval tuning — Caspian Analytics next steps

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the RAG qualification:

Summary from the call
- Primary goal: extract correct, auditable answers for analyst queries over Caspian's research corpus while minimizing hallucinations and protecting PII.
- Size and shape of data: ~1.6M documents (mix of reports, tables, PDFs), notable sections flagged as sensitive.
- Key constraints: tight latency target for interactive analyst UX (~<500ms 95th), and need for private embedding control.

Initial recommendations (high level)
- Model candidates to eval: redwood-13b-q4f (low-cost baseline) and redwood-70b-int8 (higher-quality reference).
- Retriever defaults: chunk_size=800–1200 tokens, overlap=50 tokens, embeddings: 1536-d (existing Caspian store compatible).
- Vector store: we can evaluate with your private FAISS store (see note below) and with a managed Pinecone comparison.
- Reranker: recommend a cross-encoder re-ranker for sensitivity-critical queries; fall back to a bi-encoder for latency-sensitive paths.

Grounding / quality metrics to track
- Grounded Response Rate (GRR): percent of responses citing matching doc(s).
- Hallucination rate: manual label on a prompt suite (expected threshold <= 6%).
- Precision@K (K=5) and Recall@K for retrieval layer.
- Latency distribution (p50/p95) end-to-end and reranker-only.

Artifacts we'll share
- Prompt set for the analyst UX (attachment: caspian_prompt_suite_v1.jsonl)
- Retrieval config examples (attachment: retrieval-config-examples.yaml)
- Link to Redwood benchmark harness with expected baseline numbers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evals-caspian

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm a secure S3 link or temporary read access to a 50k doc sample (sanitized) we can use for the initial bench?
2) Please confirm whether embedding generation will remain in your private environment (you mentioned a private store) or you'd like Redwood to host embeddings during the pilot.
3) Proposed timeline: data handoff week of Nov 15 -> 2-week automated eval -> sync on results week of Nov 30. Does that work?

I'll kick off a small pilot config once we have the sample and access plan. Looping in Marissa and Soojin for the eval artifacts and retrieval knobs.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Grounding sensitivity and retrieval tuning — Caspian Analytics next steps

Thanks, Lukas — this is very helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before we hand off the sample: 

1) Private embeddings: we do want to keep embedding generation inside our VPC for compliance. Is Redwood able to run retrieval/eval against our vector store when using Redwood Private, or do we need to export vectors?

2) Allowlist control: some of our docs are strictly internal (PII) and should never be surfaced. Can we apply a metadata allowlist/blocklist at the retrieval layer so those docs never get retrieved?

3) Cost ballpark: can you give a rough token/compute estimate for the two-model run you suggested (13b baseline + 70b reference) for a 50k-doc sample and a 5k-prompt suite? Procurement on CC is starting to look for SOW language.

Uploading a short data-classification summary for context (attached: caspian_data_classification_summary.pdf).

If you want, we can do the Nov 15 start but would like a day or two of runway to get procurement and our security engineer on the temporary-access flow.

—Amit
Director of Data Products
Caspian Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Patel <amit@caspiananalytics.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Grounding sensitivity and retrieval tuning — Caspian Analytics next steps

Hi Amit —

Great questions. Short answers up front: yes, and yes — both private embedding stores and metadata-level allowlists are supported in our Private deployment pattern. More detail below plus links and config examples.

Private embeddings and evaluation
- Redwood Private can be configured to query your FAISS store via a network bridge (no vector export required). For the pilot we'll ask you to set up a read-only endpoint and a temporary API key. This keeps vectors in your environment.

Retrieval allowlist/blocklist
- We can enforce document-level filters at query time using metadata tags (e.g., sensitivity: public|internal|restricted). The retrieval path will apply the filter before ranking so restricted docs are never scored or returned. We'll include an example filter in retrieval-config-examples.yaml (attached).

Reranker recommendation and tradeoffs
- For Caspian's sensitivity profile: cross-encoder reranker (small fine-tuned model we call xenc-6) gives the best grounding precision but adds ~180–300ms p95 depending on hardware.
- Option B: lightweight bi-encoder + scalar reweight (lower latency, slightly lower precision). We usually run a hybrid: cross-encoder for queries flagged as high-sensitivity, bi-encoder for exploratory queries.

Evaluation thresholds (proposed pilot gates)
- Grounded Response Rate (GRR) >= 92%
- Hallucination <= 6% (manual label target on sampled prompts)
- Precision@5 >= 78%
- End-to-end latency p95 <= 450ms (interactive path)

Artifacts and links
- Prompt suite: caspian_prompt_suite_v1.jsonl (attached) — covers 5k analyst prompts across discovery, drilldown, and table extraction.
- Retrieval config examples: retrieval-config-examples.yaml (attached) — includes chunk sizes, overlap, metadata filter examples, and reranker toggles.
- Benchmark harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evals-caspian

Cost note and ballpark
- Rough pilot estimate (50k docs, 5k prompts, 2 models): ~1200–1600 GPU hours for the full eval sweep if we run the 70b-int8 baseline on dedicated 8xA100 nodes; 13b runs on smaller nodes ~300–500 GPU hours. We can refine when you confirm exact concurrency. We'll provide a line-item SOW for procurement.

Proposed schedule
- Nov 15: secure sample + access window granted by Caspian
- Nov 16–Nov 30: automated eval run (data prep + retrieval + model inference + reranker)
- Dec 1: readout + recommendations + next-phase SOW discussion

Next steps for you
- Share readable sample S3 link or temporary FAISS endpoint credentials.
- Procurement: if you can share the person handling SOW (procurement@caspiananalytics.com is on this thread) we'll send draft SOW and estimated pricing.

I'll assign the eval run and start the template SOW. Looping Soojin if we need additional benchmarking knobs (latency targets, concurrency).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
